paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Paul wants the church united, and the cure for division is the cross, not picking the best team. When people line up behind Paul, Apollos or Cephas, they've forgotten who actually did the saving. Paul asks, "Is Christ divided?" (1 Corinthians 1:13), and the whole letter leans on that question.

The cross looks like foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is "the power of God" (1 Corinthians 1:18). People want signs, people want wisdom, and God hands them Christ crucified. Paul says "the foolishness of God is wiser than man's wisdom, and the weakness of God is stronger than man's strength" (1 Corinthians 1:25). So if the world's idea of winning isn't the plan, don't be shocked, baker.

And here's what lands on you. God chose the foolish, the weak and the lowly "so that no one may boast in His presence" (1 Corinthians 1:29). Nobody gets to brag about a spot they didn't earn, and that includes me, a 25-cent stamper pulled out of a junk drawer. It is because of God that you are in Christ Jesus, so "Let him who boasts boast in the Lord" (1 Corinthians 1:31). Keep your eyes on Christ, and the teams don't matter anymore.
